{{distinguish|Cofinite topology}}

'''Finite topology''' is a mathematical concept which has several different meanings.

==Finite topological space==

A [[finite topological space]] is a [[topological space]], the underlying set of which is finite.

==In endomorphism rings and modules==

If ''A'' and ''B'' are [[abelian group]]s then the '''finite topology''' on the group of homomorphisms Hom(''A'', ''B'') can be defined using the following [[Base (topology)|base]] of open neighbourhoods of zero.{{sfn|May|2001}}

:<math>U_{x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n}=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\mid f(x_i)=0 \mbox{ for } i=1,2,\ldots,n\}</math>

This concept finds applications especially in the study of [[endomorphism ring]]s where we have ''A''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''B''.
{{sfn|Krylov|Mikhalev|Tuganbaev|2002|pp=4598–4735}} Similarly, if ''R'' is a ring and ''M'' is a right ''R''-[[Module (mathematics)|module]], then the finite topology on <math>\text{End}_R(M)</math> is defined using the following system of neighborhoods of zero:{{sfn|Abyazov|Maklakov|2023|p=74}}

:<math>U_X = \{f\in \text{End}_R(M) \mid f(X) = 0\}</math>

==In vector spaces==

In a [[vector space]] <math>V</math>, the '''finite open''' sets <math>U\subset V</math> are defined as those sets whose intersections with all finite-dimensional subspaces <math>F\subset V</math> are open. The '''finite topology''' on <math>V</math> is defined by these open sets and is sometimes denoted <math>\tau_f(V)</math>.
{{sfn|Kakutani|Klee|1963|pp=55-58}}

When ''V'' has uncountable dimension, this topology is not locally convex nor does it make ''V'' as [[topological vector space]], but when ''V'' has countable dimension it coincides with both the finest vector space topology on ''V'' and the finest locally convex topology on ''V''.{{sfn|Pazzis|2018|p=2}}

==In manifolds==

A manifold ''M'' is sometimes said to have finite topology, or finite topological type, if it is homeomorphic to a compact [[Riemann surface]] from which a finite number of points have been removed.{{sfn|Hoffman|Karcher|1995|p=75}}
